findings.quote: The current tests are with a 10 mm thick PMMA slab in support of the Saffire II sample 9 test [15].
findings.about: Ground tests on the same 10 mm PMMA slab as Saffire-II sample 9

findings.quote: Results show that reductions of pressure slow down the flame spread over the PMMA surface approaching that in microgravity.
findings.about: Thick PMMA, concurrent flow: lowering the pressure on the ground slows flame spread toward the spread in orbit
findings.note: Ground: 100 to 40 kPa, 200 mm/s forced flow. Orbit: Saffire-II, 100 kPa, 200 mm/s (same abstract).

findings.quote: The extrapolation of the correlation to low pressures predicts well the flame spread rate obtained in microgravity in the Saffire II experiments.
findings.about: A mixed-convection correlation of the ground data, carried to low pressure, predicts the Saffire-II spread rate

findings.quote: it would be necessary to reduce the pressure to values of the order of 30 to 20 kPa to simulate microgravity conditions
findings.about: To imitate microgravity on the ground, the pressure would have to fall to about 20 to 30 kPa
findings.note: Thick PMMA in concurrent flow; the authors add that some simplifications of their analysis may not hold there.

findings.quote: As ambient pressure is progressively reduced, the flame spread characteristics get closer to what is observed in microgravity.
findings.about: Concluding remark: at lower pressure the flame looks and spreads more like the flame in orbit

findings.quote: iv The flames remain anchored at the base of the sample which has a very slow regression rate (0.01 to 0.04 mm/s).
findings.about: Thick PMMA (2-8, 2-9): flames stayed anchored at the base; regression 0.01 to 0.04 mm/s (no site variable)
findings.note: Footnote iv of Table I, given for the spread rate of samples 2-8 and 2-9.

findings.quote: iii This is the length of fuel with significant visible damage.
findings.about: Thick PMMA (2-8, 2-9): the ~10 cm burn length is the length visibly damaged

findings.quote: Initial oxygen concentration 22.1% (ISS reading, slightly higher than Saffire-1’s 21.7%)
findings.about: Saffire-II starting oxygen, as read on the ISS

findings.quote: All upward burns except Sample 2-4 was downward
findings.about: Saffire-II: all burns upward (concurrent) except 2-4, downward (opposed)

findings.quote: Average flame power: Saffire 1: 1200 +/- 300 W Saffire 2: (SIBAL fabric) 200 +/- 50 W Saffire 2: (Thick PMMA) 600 +/- 100 W
findings.about: Average flame power: Saffire-I 1200 +/- 300 W; Saffire-II fabric 200 +/- 50 W; thick PMMA 600 +/- 100 W (no site variable)
